3.  Appointment of Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference
  and General Assembly Delegate
  Annual Southern California Association of Governments Regional Conference and
  General Assembly will be held in Palm Desert, CA from May 1-2, 2025. The City’s voting
  delegate will vote on agenda items pertaining to the General Assembly —Business
  Meeting.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution appointing Mayor Ann H. Marshall as the City of Avalon voting delegate
  and Councilmember Lisa Lavelle as the alternate delegate for the Annual Southern
  California Association of Governments Regional Conference and General Assembly in
  May 2025.

4.  Resolution Approving New Classifications and Descriptions Proiect Manager, Senior
  —

  Management Analyst, and Parking Enforcement Officer
  The City of Avalon Personnel Rules and Regulations provides the City Manager the
  authority to modify and add classifications to improve the City’s administrative and
  operational organization. The City Manager proposes to add three new classifications to
  the City —  Project Manager, Senior Management Analyst, and Parking Enforcement
  Officer.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution approving new classifications and job descriptions for Project
  Manager, Senior Management Analyst, and Parking Enforcement Officer.

5.  Medical Cannabis Delivery Business Permit Aprlication Solicitation
  On August 6, 2024, the City Council authorized Staff to open the application process for
  a potential new medical cannabis delivery business permit holder. The application period
  closed on December 16, 2024 at 4 p.m. No completed applications were received by the
  deadline.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the finding that the City did not receive any completed applications for Medical
  Cannabis Delivery Services Business Permits by the stated deadline  December 16,
  —

  2024 at 4 p.m. and as such, reject all proposals. 2. Authorize City Staff to reopen the
  application process for a new medical cannabis delivery business permit holder.

 6.  2025 Waterside Permit Renewals
  Each year Prior to December, the Harbor Master reviews all existing Waterside Permits.
  Waterside Permits expire annually on December 31st. If the Harbor Master determines
  that, because of changed circumstances, a permit should not be renewed, or should be
  renewed on different terms and conditions, he shall forward his recommendation thereon
  to the City Council for action, together with a list of all permits that he recommends should
  be renewed for another term without change.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the Harbor Master to renew the attached list of Waterside Permits for 2025.

7.  Rehabilitation of City Float 1 Located at the Cabrillo Mole
  On December 17, 2019, the City Council designated Al Larson Boat Shop as a sole
  source vendor as defined in the Avalon Municipal Code section 3-4.111(b) to contract for
  repair and maintenance of certain City floats. Mole Float 1 is in need of rehabilitation to
  extend its useful life and provide safe facilities for the users. Float 1 was last rehabilitated
  in 2018.
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the affirmative finding that Al Larson Boat Shop is a sole source vendor per
  Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.111 (b). 2. Authorize the City Manager or their
  designee to negotiate a procurement contract with Al Larson Boat Shop for the
  rehabilitation of City Float I for a sum not-to-exceed $90,000.00.

GENERAL BUSINESS

8.  Cultural Resources Consultation Agreement with Montrose Environmental Services
  On November 25, 2024 the City of Avalon issued a notice to proceed to Jordahl
  Construction, Inc. to complete the Five Corners Site Improvement Project. Knowing a
  portion of the scope of work essential for this project was being completed in a designated
  culturally sensitive area, the City entered into a professional services agreement with
  Montrose Environmental Solutions, Inc. to provide on-call cultural resources consultation
  services for a not to exceed sum of $24,000. After an initial assessment of the site,
  Montrose provided a revised proposal outlining.

  Recommended Action
  1. Make an affirmative finding to dispense with a competitive procurement process due
  to economic efficiency as outlined in Avalon Municipal Code 3-4.111(c). 2. Authorize the
  City Manager to execute the First Amendment to a professional services agreement with
  Montrose Environmental Solutions, Inc., to provide cultural resource consulting for the
  Five Corner Site Improvement Project, for a not to exceed sum of $118,000.

9.  Island Enterprises, Inc. Transportation Permit Application
  On December 26, 2024 Island Enterprises, Inc. (DBA Adventure Tours) submitted an
  additional Transportation Permit Application for City tours with a 2022 Chevy 4500. Tours
  will follow the “Inside Adventure Tour” route shown in the map submitted (previously
  conducted by the General). This proposed route is entirely within the City limits.
  Recommended Action
  1. Receive presentation. 2. Discuss. 3. If consensus is met, approve the Transportation
  Permit for Island Enterprises, Inc. to utilize a commercial vehicle permit to conduct City
  tours in an oversized vehicle with stated conditions.

10.  Catalina Island Conservancy Transportation Permit Modification
  On December 11, 2024 the Catalina Island Conservancy submitted a transportation
  permit application modification to add a passenger transportation route from the Trailhead
  to the Wrigley Memorial for conservancy customers. The vehicles listed in the application
  have received prior City Council approval to conduct tours in the interior. The requested
  modification will allow for passenger transportation to/from the Trailhead and the Wrigley
  Memorial for two vans.
  Recommended Action
  1. Receive presentation. 2. Discuss. 3. If consensus is met, approve the Transportation
  Permit for Catalina Island Conservancy to utilize Commercial Interior Vehicle permits to
  conduct passenger transportation with stated conditions.

11.  Catalina Curated Tours Transportation Permit Application
  On December 31, 2024 Catalina Curated Tours submitted a transportation permit
  application to provide tours within the City of Avalon utilizing an existing residential
  autoette permit. The tour will include pick-up/drop-off in the passenger loading zone
  adjacent to Bluewater restaurant with specialized historical tour of the City.
  Recommended Action
  1. Receive presentation. 2. Discuss. 3. If consensus is met, approve the Transportation
  Permit for Catalina Curated Tours to utilize a residential autoette vehicle permit to conduct
  City tours with stated conditions.

12.  Avalon History Tours Transportation Permit Application
  On January 7, 2025 Avalon History Tours submitted a transportation permit application
  to conduct City tours in an electric vehicle. Tours will follow the route shown in the map
  submitted and is entirely within the City limits. One of the owners of the business came

  Recommended Action
  1. Receive presentation. 2. Discuss. 3. If consensus is met, approve the Transportation
  Permit for Avalon History Tours to utilize a commercial vehicle permit to conduct tours
  with stated conditions.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the Harbor Master to designate Al Larson Boat Shop
as a sole source vendor as dofined in the Avalon Municipal Code to contract repair and

REPORT SUMMARY: The City-owned and maintained public floats present particular
challenges when it comes time to safely haul them out of the water for repairs or maintenance.
Additionally, due to the size, width and weight of the City floats, transport off of the Island to
mainland facilities is required.

Al Larson Boat Shop uses a unique rail system for hauling floats and vessels out of the water.
The vessel, or float, is [bated” onto a platform, blocked and secured, and then the entire
platform is winched up the rails to its final dry dock position. This is a safer, more efficient and
cost-effective way to haul the City’s floats out of the water.

According to the AMC Sec.3-4.111(b) Sole Source Vendors, When there is only
one source that provides the necessary services, goods and equipment to ensure compatibility
with existing City services, goods or equipment, or the services, goods or equipment are
proprietary in nature, the City may procure the goods or services from the sole source.”

It is, therefore, Staff’s recommendation that Al Larson Boat Shop be utilized as a Sole Source
Vendor for maintenance and repair of the City’s floats due to their experience and ability to
safely and efficiently provide the requested services.

will continue to utilize the RFP process for City floats maintenance and repairs.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): 1. Make an affirmative finding to dispense with a
competitive procurement process due to economic efficiency as outlined in Avalon
Municipal Code 3-4.111 (c). 2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the First
Amendment to a professional services agreement with Montrose Environmental
Solutions, Inc., to provide cultural resource consulting for the Five Corner Site
Improvement Project, for a not to exceed sum of $118,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: On November 25, 2024 the City of Avalon issued a notice to
proceed to Jordahl Construction, Inc. to complete the Five Corners Site Improvement
Project (CIP Project #180003).

Knowing a portion of the scope of work essential for this project was being completed in
a designated culturally sensitive area, the City planned to contract with a cultural resource
consultant to provide on call oversight. On December 16, 2024, the City entered into a
professional services agreement with Montrose Environmental Solutions, Inc. (Montrose)
to provide on-call cultural resources consultation services for a not to exceed sum of
$24,000.

Shortly after contracting with Montrose, archeologists on site noted potentially culturally
significant items being excavated through the eastern edge of Tremont Street between
Catalina and Clarissa Avenues. After an initial assessment of the site, Montrose provided
a revised proposal outlining a scope of services to provide cultural resource monitoring
services and sediment screening as well as a final monitoring report for a total of
$1 17,889.

City Staff met with Montrose to discuss the proposal and project scope on January 16,
2025 and developed a plan to mitigate project costs while ensuring preservation and
protection of culturally significant items discovered on site.

The City previously contracted with Montrose to provide operation and maintenance
services of the City’s wastewater treatment facility from 2018 to 2023. In 2023, the
wastewater treatment facility contract was assigned to PERCWater.
 Montrose is a large corporation with a number of environmental service focuses including
cultural resource monitoring. Montrose has provided cultural resource monitoring
services on Catalina Island for a number of other entities and projects including Southern
California Edison. Montrose also employs an Avalon resident Gabe Robles, as a Project
Professional.

With Montrose currently engaged in the Five Corner Site Improvement project, the City
will not gain a competitive advantage by using a formal contract bid or other competitive
procedure. If the City were to attempt to implement a competitive process the delay will
result in construction cost overruns with the contractor. City Staff recommend City Council
make the affirmative finding to dispense with a competitive procurement process due to
economic efficiency as outlined in the Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-4.1 11(c).

Staff recommends the City Council authorizes the City Manager to execute the First
Amendment to a professional services agreement with Montrose Environmental
Solutions, Inc., to provide cultural resource consulting for the Five Corner Site
Improvement Project, fora not to exceed sum of $118,000.

FISCAL IMPACTS: These contracted services will be allocated to Fiscal Year 2024-25
Capital Improvement Program Project #1 80003, account #10575-6547.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will not
be in compliance with cultural monitoring required for the Five Corners Site Improvement
Project and may incur cost overruns associated with the construction project.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute contract amendment.
